ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Frederick Cook Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: New patient visit to establish care after release from prison: history, medication reconciliation, blood pressure, a right carotid bruit, re-entry screening for hepatitis C, tuberculosis and HIV, mood and social needs, and a vascular neurology referral. Concerns: He worries that people will recognize him and that his conviction and the disputes over his claims will follow him to every landlord and employer; He wants to stay well enough to finish his memoirs, and he does not want to depend on anyone. [S]

tr.td: Resting twelve-lead electrocardiogram: sinus rhythm, 72 per minute, normal axis and intervals, no left ventricular hypertrophy by voltage, no Q waves

Duplex ultrasound of both carotid arteries: right internal carotid peak systolic velocity 165 cm/s, end-diastolic velocity 38 cm/s, internal-to-common carotid ratio 2.6, heterogeneous plaque, consistent with 50 to 69 percent stenosis; left internal carotid peak systolic velocity 96 cm/s with less than 50 percent plaque; both vertebral arteries with antegrade flow
Advance care planning conversation, about 20 minutes

Transthoracic echocardiogram: normal left ventricular size and wall thickness, no left ventricular hypertrophy, ejection fraction about 60 percent, normal diastolic function for age, mild aortic valve sclerosis without stenosis

list.item: Elevated blood pressure at the first visit, 166/94 mmHg (average of two seated readings), without a previous diagnosis of hypertension; no symptoms; out-of-office confirmation with a week of home readings requested: resolved, confirmed [S]

Right carotid bruit heard at the first visit in a man with no symptoms of stroke or transient ischemic attack; carotid duplex ultrasound and vascular neurology consultation requested: resolved, confirmed [S]

Asymptomatic atherosclerotic stenosis of the right internal carotid artery, 50 to 69 percent by duplex ultrasound, with less than 50 percent plaque on the left; no stroke or transient ischemic attack; managed with best medical therapy (blood pressure control, a statin and low-dose aspirin) and yearly duplex surveillance: active, confirmed [S]

Recent release from about six years of incarceration: re-entering community life on parole at 65, establishing primary care with no medical records yet received, a rented room, no earned income, and a public reputation he feels as a burden: active, confirmed [S]

list.item: Released on parole four months ago after about six years in custody (county jail, then a federal penitentiary), where he worked in the prison hospital and edited the prison newspaper; reports monthly to a parole officer [S]
Trained as a physician; led and served on polar expeditions; no longer practices; writing his memoirs [S]
Rents a furnished room by the week; no earned income; part of any earnings goes toward a court-ordered fine; has applied for Social Security retirement benefits and Medicare [S]
Tobacco: never. Alcohol: none since before prison; no other drugs, no injection drug use, no tattoos received in prison [S]
Walks for an hour most days; ate prison food for years and now cooks on a hot plate; has no car [S]

tr.td: New patient visit to establish care after release from prison: history, medication reconciliation, blood pressure, a right carotid bruit, re-entry screening for hepatitis C, tuberculosis and HIV, mood and social needs, and a vascular neurology referral
Two-week follow-up: home blood pressure readings, carotid duplex ultrasound and vascular neurology consultation, starting treatment
Six-week review: blood pressure, electrolytes and kidney function on hydrochlorothiazide and amlodipine; statin and aspirin tolerance
Twelve-week review: blood pressure and lipids after a gout flare on hydrochlorothiazide; switch to losartan
Sixteen-week review: blood pressure, potassium and kidney function on losartan, mood, social needs and stroke prevention
Initial preventive physical examination (Welcome to Medicare)
Same-day sick visit for a painful, swollen right big toe

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Vascular neurology consultation in two weeks, with carotid duplex ultrasound before it, for a right carotid bruit in a man with high blood pressure: degree of stenosis, medical therapy or revascularization, and surveillance
Home blood pressure monitoring twice daily for seven days with a validated upper-arm cuff, to confirm or exclude hypertension before treatment; lower salt, the DASH eating pattern, and daily walking

Baseline tests: basic metabolic panel, HbA1c, lipid panel, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, TSH, hemoglobin and ALT, and a resting ECG; re-entry screening with a hepatitis C antibody, an interferon-gamma release assay for latent tuberculosis, an HIV test and a hepatitis B panel; PHQ-9
GL-AHA-HTN-2025, GL-CMID-2026, GL-USPSTF-HCV-2020, GL-CDC-HCV-2020, GL-USPSTF-LTBI-2023, GL-CDC-TB-CORR-2006, GL-USPSTF-DEP-2023

Re-entry support: a release-of-information request for his prison medical records, a social work referral for housing, Social Security and Medicare enrollment, a low-cost pharmacy plan, and a conversation about shame and reputation, with follow-up of mood at each visit
Two first-line drugs for stage 2 hypertension, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg and amlodipine 5 mg daily, aiming for below 130/80 mmHg, with sodium, potassium and creatinine in about four weeks

Best medical therapy for asymptomatic right carotid stenosis of 50 to 69 percent: atorvastatin 40 mg and aspirin 81 mg daily, a lipid panel and ALT in 4 to 12 weeks, blood pressure control, stroke warning signs and calling 911, and a repeat duplex in twelve months
Switch hydrochlorothiazide to losartan 50 mg daily after a drug-induced gout flare, with potassium and creatinine one to two weeks after starting; no urate-lowering drug after a single flare
Office and home blood pressure below 130/80 mmHg by four months
LDL cholesterol lowered by at least half on a statin
LDL 68 mg/dL, from 148 mg/dL, on atorvastatin 40 mg
Knows the warning signs of stroke and to call 911 at once
Taught and repeated back the BE FAST signs at the consultation visit
A stable room, Social Security and Medicare in place, and a health insurance card in hand
Six-month lease on his room; retirement benefits and Medicare approved

list.item: Independent in all activities of daily living and in managing money, medicines and transport [S]

Alert, articulate and dignified; guarded about his past and the public disputes over his claims; describes shame and low spirits at times but enjoys his writing; PHQ-9 score 7, no thoughts of death or self-harm [S]
